title: Coin Change
source: canonical Coin Change concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of coin values and a target amount. Return the smallest number of coins whose values sum exactly to amount, reusing values freely. Return -1 when no combination works. An amount of 0 needs 0 coins.

examples.explanation: Two 3-coins reach 6; grabbing a 4 first would waste moves on 4+1+1.
No combination of 2s lands exactly on 3.

hints: Build the answer for every amount from 0 upward, not for the target alone.
The fewest coins for amount a is one plus the fewest coins for a - c, taken over the coins c that fit.
Fill a table from 0 to amount: table[a] = min(table[a - c] + 1) over fitting coins; unreachable stays infinite.
solution: Bottom-up table over amounts 0 to target: each entry is one more than the best smaller amount reachable by spending one coin. O(n * amount) time where n is the coin count, O(amount) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include impossible amounts, an amount of 0, and values that tempt a greedy first pick

visible.failNote: the biggest coin first is not always fewest coins
exact sums only; overshoot does not count
